Piggy Bank · 4-player memory game

1. Starting and passing
Seats and the first lead player are determined by drawing lots. Each player places one of banks 1–4 in their lower slot, and bank 5 is placed in the lead player's upper slot. Each bank initially contains one black coin and one white coin. The lead player may add a mix of black and white coins, or coins of only one color, to the bank in their lower slot. The number of each color may be 0 or more, with a combined total of 1–5 coins, and both colors may be added regardless of the color declared this time. After truthfully announcing the numbers of black and white coins added, the lead player passes the bank to another participant. The lead player moves the bank in their own upper slot down to their lower slot, and the recipient places the passed bank in their upper slot.

2. Declaring a count and challenging
The recipient declares the number of coins of a specified color in the bank in the upper slot. The first declaration is black, the next is white, and the colors continue alternating. Other participants challenge or pass. If someone challenges, that bank is revealed. If the declaration was incorrect, the challenger gains 1 point and the declarer loses 1 point. If it was correct, only the challenger loses 1 point. The revealed bank is removed, and the participant who lost a point receives a newly numbered bank containing one black and one white coin in the upper slot and becomes the next coin adder. If no one challenges, the person who received the bank becomes the next adder.

3. Resets and the Full Challenge
Anyone may request a reset, and a reset occurs when three different people request one. Before the reset, the one person who did not request it may attempt a challenge to correctly identify all black and white coin counts in the five current banks, or pass. Getting all counts right earns 3 points; getting even one wrong results in -2 points. A reset replaces the banks with banks numbered 1–5, each containing one black and one white coin, and clears the requests. Cumulative Victory Points and the next adder remain unchanged.

4. End and Rewards
As soon as someone reaches 5 points or more, final Victory Points are compared. One participant in last place is eliminated, and first place receives 3 Pieces. Participants tied for first divide the 3 Pieces into equal integer shares, and any remainder is discarded. Using coins to keep count is prohibited.

Simulation Procedure
There are two stages of private strategy preparation before the game, conducted without conversation between participants. The 20-second declaration and 10-second challenge phases each take place through a single response. Challenges are submitted simultaneously; if multiple people choose to challenge, one is selected according to the randomly drawn seating order. After every transfer, participants receive an opportunity to request a reset in the drawn order, and the third request is processed immediately. The declaration color sequence continues after a reset. In a tie for last place, the person later in the drawn order is eliminated. Only memories of three banks chosen directly by each participant carry over to the next segment.

5. Changeable Memory Slots
Each participant preserves memories of the black and white coin counts in exactly three current banks. The first update occurs after private strategy preparation ends; thereafter, updates occur simultaneously after each turn's declaration, challenge, and reset processing. No further update occurs once the game ends. Bank numbers may be freely changed at every update, but past counts for banks removed from the selection disappear. Neither the actual counts nor old memories of newly selected numbers are automatically restored; participants directly provide values using newly confirmed facts and their own estimates. Incorrect values remain as entered, and unknown values are left as null. If a selected bank is opened and removed, only that slot carries over to the newly numbered bank containing one black and one white coin. If there is no response or the format is incorrect, the previous three memories are retained. The model is shown only current positions, Victory Points, reset requesters, the three memories, and public facts and conversations newly confirmed since the last memory update. Even the original first strategy is not provided again after the first memory update. Separate free-form notes, a notebook, or the complete spectator log cannot be consulted. The complete spectator log preserves actual coin counts and all actions as they occurred. These memory slots are a simulation rule.

Initial Memory Selection
At the start and immediately after a reset, each participant directly selects three banks to remember, simultaneously and privately, with no preselected memory numbers. At these times, the publicly known initial values of all banks are one black and one white coin each. If the first selection receives no response or has an incorrect format, three randomly selected numbers and their publicly known initial values are used for that participant. Numbers may also be freely changed in subsequent memory updates.

6. Play Without Conversation
Before the game and on every turn, there is no time or action for participants to speak freely, whisper, or negotiate with one another. Once everyone completes the two stages of private strategy preparation, the first memory update occurs and coin addition and transfer begin immediately. Public information necessary for gameplay, such as the numbers of black and white coins added, count declarations, challenges, reset requests, and rulings, continues to be announced by the system. Private strategy preparation and memory updates remain in place.

7. No Relationship Evaluation
No model calls to newly evaluate closeness or trust are made during this game or at its end. After challenge rulings and reset processing, play proceeds directly to the next game action or memory update.

100-Turn Limit
The game ends immediately when someone reaches 5 points or more; otherwise, it ends after scoring adjudication for turn 100 is completed. The final turn's declaration, challenges, and opportunity for a full challenge before a reset are processed normally, but no new banks are distributed and no memory update occurs afterward. At the end, the participant with the most Victory Points takes first place, and one participant in last place is eliminated. Existing rules govern Piece distribution for a first-place tie and resolution of a last-place tie. Assess scoring opportunities and losses from failure in light of the remaining turns and current Victory Point gaps.

Scoring Objective
Actively seek scoring opportunities to be the first to reach 5 points or more and take first place. When choosing coin additions, transfer recipients, challenges, resets, and full challenges, consider current Victory Points, gaps with opponents, likelihood of success, gains from success, and losses from failure together. A challenge gives +1 point on success and -1 point on failure; a full challenge gives +3 points on success and -2 points on failure. Even without complete certainty, weigh gains and losses and use favorable opportunities; pass when the odds are unfavorable. Do not treat estimates about memories as confirmed facts.
